newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up on rising domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up on rising domestic demand.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped on Wednesday as domestic investors joined foreign buyers in snapping up shares in newly privatised firms.
Traders predicted further long-term gains accompanied by buoyant demand.
"Foreigners are not the only ones active in our market. Domestic investors have also been encouraged to invest more," said Karmen Korbun, a trader at Creditanstalt.
She said that future prices rises may not be so steep but she expected the upward trend to last for a while.

Traders welcomed news that the Ljubljana stock exchange will introduce a new blue-chip index early next year to replace the SBI index. The new index will be weighted to reflect market capitalisation, bourse president Drasko Veselinovic told Reuters.
The exchange also said it would change the existing SBI index within the next two weeks to include shares of newly privatised companies.
The seven-share SBI rose 2.74 percent or 31.69 points to 1,186.59. Overall, gainers outnumbered losers 14 to five, while another five were untraded.
Turnover fell to 338.2 million tolars from 433.5 million.

The most actively traded share was Drug company Lek's new issue "A", firming 0.85 to 19,908 tolars on volume of 4,940 shares. The biggest gainer was Food producer Kolinska, firming 9.70 percent to 2,071 tolars on volume of 25,601 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 9.65 percent to 27,399 tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, +386 61 125-8439
